result.title: RFP NUMBER 23-09
result.summary: Request for Proposals 23-09 seeks alternative investment consulting services. Released October 23, 2023; inquiries are due November 13, 2023, at 3:00 p.m. EST, and proposals by December 15, 2023, at 3:00 p.m. EST. The document covers the introduction, INPRS background, issuer and contacts, inquiry and submission procedures, confidentiality, costs, proposal validity, taxes, registration, compliance, and milestones; proposal instructions, transmittal letter, business and fee proposals; scope of services; and contract award, term, and evaluation criteria. Appendices include a sample investment consulting agreement and essential clauses, mandatory taxpayer identification and foreign registration forms, and a questionnaire.

result.title: Section 1 – Introduction
result.summary: Introduces INPRS’s RFP for alternative investment consulting covering absolute return, private credit, private equity, and real assets; INPRS prefers one broadly expert consultant but may split asset classes. It describes INPRS’s statutory role, $39.6 billion in assets, investment targets and alternative portfolios, investment staff, systems, and the consultant’s close work with the Investment Department. It sets procurement rules: questions and submissions go only to the designated procurement contact by stated deadlines; addenda, clarifications, corrections, withdrawals, and possible disqualification are governed by the RFP. Proposal records are generally public under Indiana law, with procedures for claiming confidentiality and providing redacted copies. Respondents bear proposal costs and taxes, must maintain proposals for at least 180 days, and out-of-state corporations must register before contract discussions. Respondents certify compliance with Indiana legal and payment obligations; INPRS may investigate and impose remedies for liabilities. The section also provides the solicitation timeline, from October 2023 release through March 2024 negotiations.

nodes.summary:
Section 1 – Introduction
1.1 Title
Request for Proposals (“RFP”) for Alternative Investment Consulting Services for the Indiana Public Retirement System (“INPRS” or the “System”).
1.2 Overview of Request for Consulting Services
INPRS is soliciting proposals from all qualified firms who wish to be considered as a vendor to provide Alternative Investment Consulting Services, which includes Absolute Return (Hedge Funds), Private Credit, Private Equity, and Real Asset strategies described in Section 2 - Scope of Services. INPRS prefers to contract with a single investment consultant firm with broad Alternative Investment expertise; however, INPRS may consider carving out specific asset classes in order to contract with investment consulting firms that provide exemplary expertise and thoughtfulness in an identified area.

nodes.title: 1.3 INPRS Background
key_items: Section 1 – Introduction; 1.1 Title; 1.2 Overview of Request for Consulting Services
1.2 Overview of Request for Consulting Services
nodes.summary: Established by Indiana statute in 2011, INPRS is an independent governmental instrumentality managing retirement funds for public employees. It administers 16 defined-benefit, defined-contribution, OPEB, and custodial funds, and manages about $39.6 billion. Its DB assumed return is 6.25%; target allocations are public equity 20%, private markets 15%, fixed income (ex-inflation-linked) 20%, inflation-linked fixed income 15%, commodities 10%, real assets 10%, absolute return 5%, and risk parity 20% (115% total; maximum exposure 120%). DC investments include seven core options and target-date funds, totaling about $6.5 billion. Alternatives began in 2002: targets are 5% absolute return, 15% combined private credit/equity, and 10% real assets. Portfolios include absolute return ($2.6 billion; 11 funds), private credit ($1.8 billion; 26 holdings), private equity ($4.5 billion; 225 holdings), and real assets ($3.1 billion; 87 holdings), spanning global strategies. A CIO leads 21 investment professionals; systems include Bloomberg and BNY Mellon accounting/custody feeds. The RFP follows Indiana law and INPRS policy. Respondents must direct inquiries only to procurement contact Stanton Lanman by the stated deadline; unauthorized contact may disqualify them. INPRS may clarify responses and decide which questions to answer in writing, with equal access to RFP communications.

nodes.title: INPRS Investment Resources, RFP Issuance, and Contacts
nodes.summary: INPRS’s Investment Department, led by a Chief Investment Officer and supported by 21 professionals, recommends investment strategies to the Board and manages and implements them; the selected respondent will work closely with staff and follow their direction. INPRS uses investment systems such as Bloomberg, while BNY Mellon provides accounting and custody data through standard and custom daily and monthly interfaces. Transactions are generally posted on trade date for near-real-time position and cash monitoring. INPRS issues the RFP under applicable Indiana statutes and administrative policies. Respondents must direct inquiries only as permitted by Section 1.6; unauthorized contact with staff or trustees may result in disqualification. INPRS may seek clarification on responses and will provide respondents equal access to RFP-related communications.

nodes.title: 1.6 Inquiries about the RFP for INPRS
nodes.summary: RFP questions and information requests must be emailed to Stanton Lanman, Director of Vendor Management and Procurement, at procurements@inprs.in.gov by the deadlines in Section 1.16. INPRS decides whether to answer in writing; questions and answers will be posted online. Revisions or interpretations will be issued as website addenda, and the proposal deadline may be extended if needed. Proposals are due by email to the same address by December 15, 2023, at 3:00 PM EST; late submissions are rejected. Proposals may be modified or withdrawn in writing by email before the deadline. INPRS may give affected respondents five calendar days to submit written corrections for minor errors or omissions; major omissions, such as missing prices, may disqualify a proposal. Proposal materials are generally public records under Indiana’s APRA, and the RFP file may be accessed after award. Respondents claiming a statutory disclosure exception must identify it in the Transmittal.

nodes.title: Proposal Submission, Updates, and Changes
nodes.summary: Questions and responses will be posted on the INPRS website on the date specified in RFP Section 1.16. Revisions or clarifications will be issued by website addendum before the proposal deadline; the procurement director may extend the deadline if needed. Proposals must be emailed by December 15, 2023, at 3:00 PM EST, and late submissions will not be considered. Proposals may be modified or withdrawn in writing by email before the submission deadline; later changes or withdrawals will not be accepted. At its discretion, INPRS may give affected respondents five calendar days after notification to submit written corrections for minor errors or omissions. Major omissions, such as missing prices, are not minor and may disqualify a proposal.

nodes.title: 1.9 Confidential Information
nodes.summary: Proposal materials are generally public records under Indiana’s APRA and may be inspected or copied after award. Respondents claiming a statutory disclosure exception must identify it in the Transmittal Letter, label confidential documents in filenames, and provide separate redacted public versions. INPRS decides confidentiality and may consult the Public Access Counselor (PAC); respondents may challenge determinations with the PAC and are encouraged to follow its guidance. INPRS does not reimburse proposal-preparation or other anticipated-award costs. Proposals must remain open for at least 180 days after the due date; proposals accepted for negotiations remain valid until replaced by a contract or rejected. INPRS is tax-exempt, but respondents remain responsible for taxes imposed on them. Out-of-state corporate respondents must register with the Indiana Secretary of State before doing business with INPRS; registration information is available from its Corporations Division at 302 West Washington Street, E018, Indianapolis, IN 46204, (317) 232-6576.

nodes.title: Proposal Confidentiality, Costs, Validity, and Taxes
nodes.summary: Confidential documents must be identified in filenames, with a separate redacted public-release version provided. INPRS decides confidentiality and may seek Public Access Counselor guidance; respondents may challenge its determination with the PAC and are encouraged to consult its procurement redaction guidance. INPRS is not responsible for proposal preparation or other costs incurred in anticipation of a contract. Proposals must remain open for at least 180 days after the due date; proposals accepted for negotiations remain valid until replaced by a contract or rejected. INPRS is tax-exempt and will not pay taxes imposed on respondents under a resulting contract.

nodes.title: 1.13 Secretary of State Registration
nodes.summary: Out-of-state corporate respondents must register with the Indiana Secretary of State before contract discussions, though registration is not required to submit an RFP response. Registration forms and contact details are provided, with an online link in Appendix B.2. INPRS may hold oral or written discussions with viable respondents and seek clarifications. Responses certify that the respondent and its principals have no outstanding Indiana criminal, civil, or enforcement actions or overdue taxes and other required payments; respondents must promptly report new actions. INPRS may conduct background checks and, if liabilities are found, bar contracting, cancel contracts, offset or withhold payments, and suspend purchases until payment is made and documented. The anticipated schedule is: RFP release October 23, 2023; inquiries due November 13 at 3 p.m. EST; answers November 27; submissions due December 15 at 3 p.m. EST; finalist presentations January–February 2024; finalist selection February 2024; and contract negotiations March 2024.

nodes.title: Discussion Procedures and Compliance Certification
nodes.summary: Respondents must register before contract discussions, using the application form or the online address in Appendix B.2; registration is not required to submit a response. INPRS may hold oral or written discussions with respondents it considers viable for award and seek clarifications. By responding, respondents certify that they and their principals have no outstanding Indiana criminal, civil, or enforcement actions and are current on taxes, fees, and other required payments. They must promptly notify INPRS if actions arise. INPRS may conduct background checks and, if liabilities are found, bar the respondent from contracting, cancel contracts, offset obligations against payments, or suspend payments and purchases until the liability is paid and proof is submitted.

result.title: Section 2 – Proposal Content Requirements
result.summary: Proposals must follow the prescribed electronic format and include a transmittal letter, business proposal, fee proposal, and Appendix B documents. The letter identifies the RFP and respondent, summarizes capability and proposal contents, affirms acceptance of contract terms, and is signed by an authorized representative with proof of authority; confidentiality claims require itemized legal grounds and a redacted public version. The business proposal covers services, experience, personnel, organizational capacity, registration status, two years of financial statements and the latest audit, completed Appendix C, contract exceptions and proposed language, and all assumptions and INPRS responsibilities. The fee proposal must detail a fixed U.S.-dollar price for all services and costs, guaranteed for the contract term and paid in arrears; incomplete pricing disqualifies, and Appendix A.1 clauses are non-negotiable. The RFP also describes alternative-investment consulting duties and related obligations. Contracts run five years, with optional renewals up to ten years total. INPRS evaluates compliance, financial strength, expertise, qualifications, completeness, references, experience, fees, presentations, and other factors, and may interview finalists, negotiate, reject, split, or make no award.

nodes.title: SECTION 3 – SCOPE OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: Section 3 sets minimum qualifications and the scope for INPRS’s alternative-investment consulting services. Respondents must be registered investment advisers with at least five years’ firm experience, qualifying public-pension clients and senior consultants, and must disclose conflicts, revenue sources, and affiliations; charge fixed fees; act as fiduciaries under Indiana law; and comply with applicable Indiana investment law. INPRS seeks a non-discretionary consultant for absolute return, private credit, private equity, and real assets, favoring broad capability but permitting specialist awards. The consultant must demonstrate public-pension expertise, independence, risk awareness, cultural fit, innovation, strong teams, and competitive fees, and report separately by allocation. At the Board’s discretion, services include policy and strategy development and annual review, meetings, research, fiduciary diligence, recommendations and approval materials, benchmarking, fee comparisons, negotiation support, and ongoing monitoring and compliance. Duties also cover quarterly performance, holdings, exposure, peer, benchmark, and fee reporting; education, research, special projects, database access, and seven-year record retention; hedge-fund strategy, allocation, monthly and beta/alpha analysis, tactical advice, and oversight; and private-market investment, valuation, return, commitment, and portfolio reporting, document review, and manager-discussion records. INPRS may negotiate, reject, split, or make no award, as determined by its Executive Director or designee.

nodes.title: 3.1 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Respondents must, by the response due date, meet these minimum qualifications: be a Registered Investment Advisor under the Investment Company Act of 1940, evidenced by Form ADV Parts I and II; have at least five years of investment consulting experience as a firm; serve at least two public pension fund clients, each with an alternative-investment portfolio of at least $2 billion, including absolute return/hedge funds, private credit, private equity, and real assets; and assign primary consultants with at least five years of relevant senior advisory experience for public pension plans, including investment policy, allocation implementation, and manager evaluations and recommendations. Firms must disclose conflicts or potential conflicts, revenue sources, and affiliations, particularly those involving recommended managers; charge fixed fees rather than a percentage of assets under advisement; agree to act as fiduciaries under applicable Indiana law; and comply with Indiana law applicable to INPRS investments.

nodes.title: 3.2 ALTERNATIVE INVESTMENT CONSULTING SCOPE OF SERVICE
nodes.summary: INPRS seeks a non-discretionary alternative investment consultant for Absolute Return, Private Credit, Private Equity, and Real Assets, preferably one broadly capable firm but allowing specialist awards. The consultant must demonstrate extensive public-pension experience, cultural fit, independence, risk awareness, innovation, strong teams, and competitive fees; it will work with separate staff and report by allocation. At the Board’s discretion, it will help develop and annually review policies, objectives, strategies, and pacing, attend requested ad hoc meetings, and provide manager research, fiduciary-standard diligence, recommendations, approval materials, benchmark and fee comparisons, negotiation support, and ongoing compliance practices. Services include quarterly monitoring and performance, holdings, exposure, benchmarks, peer, and fee reporting; education, research, special projects, database access, and seven-year record retention. Hedge-fund services include independent strategy and allocation analysis, monthly reporting, beta/alpha analysis, tactical advice, and manager oversight. Private-market services include detailed investment, valuation, return, benchmark, vintage, sector, geography, and commitment reporting, document review, and manager-discussion records. INPRS retains discretion to negotiate, reject, split, or make no award, with final determination by its Executive Director or designee.

nodes.title: Mandatory Services
nodes.summary: INPRS seeks a non-discretionary alternative investment consultant for its large public pension system, providing specialty advice across Absolute Return (Hedge Funds), Private Credit, Private Equity, and Real Assets. The consultant will work with separate internal teams and report separately for each allocation. Desired qualities include cultural alignment, willingness to challenge ideas and engage as a strategic partner, innovative thinking, risk awareness, a deep and diverse team, and competitive fees. Respondents must demonstrate extensive experience and superior capability. INPRS prefers one firm with broad expertise but may award specific asset classes to firms with exceptional expertise. At the Board’s discretion and under Investment Guidelines, the consultant will help develop and review alternative investment policies, objectives, and guidelines, and at least annually review strategy, objectives, and guidelines and recommend investment pacing. Meetings and availability are also identified as a service area.

nodes.title: Alternative Investment Consultant Criteria and Policies
nodes.summary: INPRS’s Alternative Investments cover Absolute Return (Hedge Funds), Private Credit, Private Equity, and Real Assets, each supported by separate staff requiring separate consultant interaction and reporting. The consultant should align with INPRS’s culture, challenge ideas and processes, be innovative and risk-conscious, act as an engaged strategic partner, offer a deep and diverse team, and provide competitive fees. Firms must demonstrate extensive experience and strong capabilities serving large public pension programs. The consultant will work with investment staff in a non-discretionary role. INPRS prefers one firm with broad expertise but may carve out asset classes for exceptional specialists. At the Board’s discretion and under Investment Guidelines, the consultant will help develop and review investment policies, objectives, and guidelines, and at least annually review strategy, objectives, and guidelines and recommend investment pacing.

nodes.title: 3.2.2 Interaction: Meetings and Availability
nodes.summary:
3.2.2 Interaction: Meetings and Availability
- 13 -1. Attend ad-hoc meetings at the request of INPRS Investment Staff. Ad-hoc meetings may be via teleconference, in-person, or virtual meeting as deemed appropriate by INPRS Investment Staff.

nodes.title: 3.2.3 Investment Manager Diligence and Compliance
nodes.summary: The Consultant will work with INPRS Investment Staff to identify and recommend opportunities aligned with market conditions, INPRS’s capabilities, investment policy, and long-term objectives. Responsibilities include creating a structured process to assess institutional-quality managers and providing access to a global alternative-manager database covering philosophy, organization, expertise, vehicles, and performance. The Consultant will develop and apply fiduciary-standard due diligence methods with INPRS staff, prepare materials for approving authorities, and provide investment/manager, operational, and quantitative reports, including benchmark and fee comparisons. INPRS staff may join requested diligence trips. The Consultant will assist with contract negotiations alongside legal counsel and seek investment capacity and favorable fees, liquidity, and redemption terms. It will also recommend policy-compliance best practices and strategies for implementing and documenting ongoing compliance procedures.

nodes.title: 3.2.4 Reporting and Monitoring
nodes.summary: Provide quarterly oversight and ongoing monitoring for all INPRS alternative investment managers, including estimated and final quarter-to-date and fiscal year-to-date returns; individual and aggregated holdings with current metrics; performance-driver and forward-positioning commentary; portfolio composition and objectives; sector and strategy outlooks; model portfolio updates; country-level geographic exposure; and benchmark reviews and optimization. Assist with selecting and developing portfolio-, strategy-, and sub-strategy-level benchmarks, including private- and public-market equivalents, and provide peer-universe analysis. Annually analyze management fees, carried interest, and expenses, reconcile fees, identify managers outside agreed deviation bands, and confirm charges align with contractual terms. Provide access to a performance-information database.

nodes.title: 3.2.5 Research and Projects
nodes.summary:
3.2.5 Research and Projects
1. Provide educational meetings/forums, training, research, and reports to INPRS Investment Staff and/or Board of Trustees as requested by INPRS Investment Staff.
2. Make available all firm research, including proprietary research, and provide consultative opportunities with research staff as requested by INPRS Investment Staff.
3. The Consultant may be required to perform other special projects and services in connection with, and in the general nature of, the above duties.
- 15 -4. The Consultant will retain account records for a period of seven (7) years and provide to INPRS a quarterly batch download or transfer via an agreed upon method of account data records.

nodes.title: Criteria Specific to Absolute Return (Hedge Funds)
nodes.summary: The Consultant will provide ongoing independent analysis and advice on Absolute Return strategies and investment vehicles; annually assess portfolio allocation, alpha and beta, returns and volatility, and recommend reallocations. Monthly performance reports will include estimated and final quarter-to-date and fiscal year-to-date returns, exposures, return attribution, and portfolio changes. Services also include a platform to distinguish alpha from traditional and alternative betas; ad hoc advice on tactical opportunities, INPRS staff processes, managed account providers and oversight, and trading strategies; and protecting INPRS’s investor interests by engaging managers and funds to ensure compliance with contract terms.

nodes.title: Criteria Specific to Private Equity, Private Credit, and Real Assets
nodes.summary: The Consultant must provide quarter-to-date and fiscal year-to-date estimated and final reports, with INPRS-designated sub-portfolios and separate Real Assets, Private Equity, and Private Credit reporting. Reports must detail each investment’s commitments, fund size, ownership, vintage, invested capital, quarter-end valuation, distributions, total value, and unfunded commitments, using partnership statements and custodian data while assessing data quality and flagging concerns. They must include gross and net IRRs; TVPI, RVPI, and DPI over multiple periods; benchmark comparisons and peer-vintage performance; vintage-year allocation and returns; sector or property-type reporting; country-level geographic exposure; and unfunded commitments. The Consultant must review fund-document amendments and recommend actions, and maintain accessible notes of manager discussions and relevant updates. INPRS may select the most advantageous proposal, make no award, negotiate or clarify proposals, reject any or all, award without discussions, or split the contract among multiple respondents. If contracting with the selected respondent fails, INPRS may approach the next qualified respondent or make no award. The Executive Director or designee makes the final discretionary determination.

nodes.title: 4.1 Length of Contract
nodes.summary:
4.1 Length of Contract
The term of the contract entered under this RFP shall be for an initial period of five (5) years, beginning from the date of final execution of contract. There may be one (1) or more renewals under the same terms and conditions at INPRS’s option up to the length of the original term. Total contract period shall not exceed ten (10) years.

nodes.title: 4.2 Evaluation Criteria
nodes.summary: INPRS has appointed qualified personnel to evaluate proposals and may select the proposal it considers most advantageous, based on all evaluation factors and other material considerations. Proposals will be assessed for the respondent’s ability to meet requirements efficiently and cost-effectively. Criteria include RFP compliance, financial strength, vendor expertise and competencies, qualifications, response quality and completeness, references, experience and track record, fee proposal, finalist presentation quality, and other relevant factors identified by INPRS. References may be contacted, and finalists may be interviewed by participants in the selection process.

result.title: Appendix A – Sample INVESTMENT CONSULTING AGREEMENT
result.summary: Appendix A presents the proposed investment consulting agreement and instructions for reviewing it: respondents must identify and explain required or desired amendments, while specified clauses are non-negotiable and unacceptable changes may disqualify a proposal; pricing should account for liability risks. Mandatory provisions address audits, legal and ethical compliance, confidentiality and public records, disputes, drug-free workplaces, Indiana law and venue, sovereign immunity, contractor liability and indemnification, nondiscrimination, MBE/WBE opportunities, records, and investigations. INPRS also rejects provisions requiring System insurance or indemnity, non-Indiana law or venue, mandatory non-court dispute resolution, taxes, penalties or fees, altered claim periods, advance payment (except rent), or unlawful disclosure limits. An acknowledgement and signature fields precede a sample five-year agreement, renewable in writing up to ten years, then month-to-month for up to six months. The agreement covers services, fees, fiduciary duties, reporting, records, audits, transition and termination; confidentiality, data, staffing, insurance, compliance, conflicts, liability, remedies, payment, and notices; and contract administration, regulatory, workplace, MBE/WBE, and anti-collusion requirements, with signature blocks.

nodes.title: Appendix A – Sample INVESTMENT CONSULTING AGREEMENT (intro)
nodes.summary: Appendix A provides the base investment consulting agreement expected if an award is made. Respondents should review it and submit proposed amendments with their business proposal, identifying each change as required or desired and explaining why. Required changes unacceptable to INPRS may make a proposal unacceptable; Appendix A.1 clauses are non-negotiable. All solicitation exceptions must be clearly identified and explained, or INPRS may disregard them; exceptions may harm evaluation. Respondents should price for liability risks from non-negotiable terms. These clauses cover: audits; legal and ethics compliance; confidentiality and Social Security disclosures; disputes (no advance binding resolution except Indiana courts, though later ADR may be considered); drug-free workplaces; Indiana governing law, venue, and sovereign immunity; contractor indemnification and liability, with no System indemnity; minority/women-owned business subcontractor bidding opportunities; nondiscrimination; legally required records retention and inspection; and investigations and complaints. The System rejects substantive or material changes to specified clauses and limits changes to others as described.

nodes.title: Additional contract provisions to which the System will not agree:
Acknowledgement
nodes.summary: The section provides an acknowledgement and signature fields confirming agreement to INPRS’s mandatory contract provisions, followed by a sample five-year investment consulting agreement, renewable in writing up to a ten-year maximum and then month to month for up to six months. It covers consulting services, incorporated duties and fee schedules, definitions, fiduciary standards, performance and reporting, meetings, records, audits, error correction, transition, and termination. Other provisions address intellectual property, confidentiality and personal data; consultant representations, staffing, registration, insurance, legal and ethical compliance, conflicts, indemnification, remedies, force majeure, notices, Indiana law, disputes, and payment. It also specifies notice contacts; funding-based cancellation; contract interpretation, completeness, severability, waivers, assignment, and delegation; drug-free workplace duties and sanctions; compliance audits; signatory authority and approval for extra work; non-debarment and counsel eligibility; liability limits, prompt payment, MBE/WBE requirements, regulatory filings, and anti-collusion attestations. Signature blocks are provided for both parties.

nodes.title: THIS INVESTMENT CONSULTING AGREEMENT
nodes.summary: The agreement is between the Indiana Public Retirement System (INPRS) and a designated Consultant, effective on a specified date. INPRS seeks, and the Consultant agrees to provide, absolute return, private equity, private credit, or real assets consulting services for INPRS’s portfolio. The agreement runs for five years from the effective date, unless changed or ended in writing; the parties may renew it in writing under Section 20, but the total term cannot exceed ten years. After expiration, it automatically renews month to month for up to six months unless modified, terminated, or renewed in writing. INPRS will pay, and the Consultant will accept as full compensation, fees mutually agreed by the parties, initially according to the incorporated fee schedule in Exhibit B.

nodes.title: 4. Definitions, Gender and Number

nodes.title: I. Fund Records (intro)
nodes.summary: Defines the fiduciary Standard of Care and Fund Records, including asset-related transaction, operational, financial, proprietary, and electronic records. INPRS appoints Consultant as fiduciary, and Consultant accepts; it and its agents must meet the expert-care standard and are liable for related claims. Consultant may serve others or pursue competing ventures. Its agency is limited to asset consulting; no employment, partnership, or joint venture is created, and its service providers are its employees. Consultant must provide mutually agreed, officer-certified reports, though it is not responsible for others’ supplied information; attend requested performance and strategy meetings and answer questions without extra charge; invoice quarterly in arrears for completed work; and invite INPRS to generally available client seminars subject to ethics rules. Termination provisions cover INPRS’s 30-day or immediate protective termination, Consultant’s termination after uncured breach and 90-day notice, accrued and final prorated fees, record retention, a transition of up to three months, pending work, and transfer cooperation; remedies are cumulative and prior claims survive. Consultant indemnifies INPRS for specified misconduct, breaches, and violations; indemnity survives termination, while INPRS does not indemnify Consultant. The text begins Consultant’s representations, warranties, and covenants.

nodes.title: A. Authorization
nodes.summary: The consultant represents that it has authority to enter the agreement, which is binding subject to bankruptcy and equitable limitations, and that signing or performing it violates no law, order, or agreement. Services must meet contractual and attached-document standards, with errors or omissions promptly corrected at INPRS’s request. The consultant warrants it has not used contingent-fee solicitors except bona fide employees, affiliates, or established agencies; breach permits immediate termination and recovery or deduction of the fee. It has not offered and will not offer gratuities to INPRS or Indiana officials or employees to influence award, performance, or continuation; violations may result in termination on one calendar day’s written notice. The consultant must not knowingly use or provide infringing intellectual property or others’ trade secrets. It must notify INPRS in writing within three business days if any contractual representation, warranty, or covenant ceases to be materially true.

nodes.title: Consultant Obligations and Contract Protections
nodes.summary: The text states that the Consultant’s agreement does not violate applicable legal constraints or other obligations. The Consultant must not offer or give gratuities to INPRS or State of Indiana personnel to obtain the contract or favorable treatment; violations may result in termination on one calendar day’s written notice. The Consultant must not knowingly develop, provide, or use materials or assets that infringe others’ intellectual property rights or constitute their trade secrets.

result.title: APPENDIX C – QUESTIONNAIRE
result.summary: Appendix C is a required questionnaire for firms seeking to provide alternative-investment consulting services to INPRS. It gathers firm history, contacts, structure, consulting experience, offices, staffing, affiliates, litigation and regulatory status, business lines, assets, revenues, clients, discretionary status, investment-management and broker-dealer activities, third-party payments, compensation, conflicts, fiduciary acknowledgment, and insurance. Firms describe teams, expertise, proposed INPRS personnel and support, capacity, technology, continuity, training, incentives, and business recovery, and report client changes, major clients, and institutional references. The questionnaire also covers client and discretionary assets, investment philosophy, portfolio construction and allocation, tools and analytics, manager searches and due diligence, reporting, fees, opportunity allocation, conflicts, and oversight. Asset-specific questions address strategy, diversification, outlook, pension-fund positioning, international exposure, manager experience and relationships, closed-fund access, discounts, and benchmarking across alternative asset classes. ESG policies and their role are covered, along with requested work samples, models, reviews, database counts, regulatory filings, team biographies, ethics, insurance, and organizational materials.

nodes.title: Indiana Public Retirement System Alternative Investment Consulting Services
nodes.summary: Appendix C is a required questionnaire for firms proposing alternative-investment consulting services to INPRS. It requests firm and primary-contact details; history and anticipated structural changes; consulting experience, offices, staffing, affiliates, litigation, regulatory status, business lines, AUM/AUA, revenues, client counts, and discretionary status. It asks about investment-management or broker-dealer activities, client assets by type and year, third-party payments, compensation and conflicts, fiduciary acknowledgment, and insurance. Respondents describe team relationships, professional headcount, tenure, and expertise by function and asset class; identify the proposed INPRS team, roles, offices, backup, quality controls, support, and communication. Further topics include growth and capacity limits, technology, expansion or restructuring plans, staff incentives and departures, training, business recovery, and key-staff continuity. Firms must report client terminations and additions since June 2018, their ten largest clients and service details, and five public-pension or institutional references.

nodes.title: REFERENCE
nodes.summary: The section requests client references, discretionary-client and asset information, the firm’s investment philosophy and value to INPRS, allocation and portfolio-construction recommendations, and average alternative-asset allocations. It covers due-diligence and reporting platforms, analytics, data, exposure aggregation, customized reports, search and peer tools, AI/ML partnerships, manager coverage, historical reviews and recommendations, manager screening and selection, diligence processes, staff and client interaction, fees, opportunity allocation, conflicts, and ongoing oversight. It asks asset-specific questions on portfolio design, diversification, outlook and alpha, pension-fund roles and tactical positioning, international exposure, manager evaluation, investment experience, closed-fund access and fee discounts, benchmarking, and major manager/GP relationships for absolute return, private equity, private credit, and real assets. ESG policies, commitments, teams, and their influence on processes are addressed. Requested exhibits include recommendation and portfolio reports, pacing models, advisory-board and GP reviews, database counts, Form ADV and registration history, proposed account-team biographies, ethics code, insurance certificates, and organizational chart.

nodes.title: REFERENCE (intro)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests client references and details on discretionary clients and assets; the firm’s philosophy, value to INPRS, recommended allocation changes, portfolio construction, and average allocations across alternative asset classes. It asks about online due-diligence and reporting tools, analytics and metrics, reporting frequency and data sources, exposure aggregation, customized reports, searches, peer rankings, and AI/ML partnerships. It seeks manager and fund coverage counts, historical opportunity-review and recommendation totals by category, and the firm’s manager evaluation, selection, database, verification, screening, and on-site diligence processes. It also addresses staff involvement, diligence timelines, consultant-client interaction, fee negotiations, opportunity allocation and conflicts, and oversight of performance, risk, objectives, integrity, compliance, valuation, restrictions, conflicts, and reporting. Finally, it asks how recommended portfolio changes are adopted, how trustees and staff are educated, and what distinctive services or tools the firm offers.

nodes.title: Absolute Return Consulting Services Specific Questions
nodes.summary: The text lists ten questions for an absolute-return consulting firm: its portfolio-construction approach for a low-beta, low-correlation hedge fund portfolio targeting 6.25% long-term annual returns; its outlook for hedge funds and future alpha; hedge funds’ role in public pensions and potential tactical positioning; industries or strategies it avoids; views on alternative/exotic betas and how to harvest them; manager identification and evaluation; access to closed funds and examples of client fee discounts; hedge fund benchmarking, including benchmark selection, peer comparisons, and custom benchmarks; its ten largest absolute-return manager relationships; and the capabilities of portfolio- and manager-level risk aggregation systems.

nodes.title: Private Equity and Private Credit Consulting Services Specific Questions
nodes.summary: The text requests information on private equity and private credit consulting: portfolio construction and diversification; market outlook and confidence in future manager alpha; their roles in public pension portfolios and potential tactical positioning; appropriate international exposure; and processes for identifying and evaluating fund managers. It asks about investment analysis and recommendation experience across buyout, growth, venture, special situations, direct lending, mezzanine, specialty finance, and co-investments. It also seeks capabilities and examples for accessing closed funds and securing client fee discounts; benchmarking methods, benchmark selection or development, comparisons with similar portfolios, custom benchmark experience, and recommendations for INPRS; and each asset class’s ten largest general-partner relationships.

nodes.title: Real Asset Consulting Services Specific Questions
nodes.summary: The text lists questions for a real assets consulting firm covering: portfolio construction and diversification across real estate, infrastructure, energy, timber, agriculture, and other real assets; industry trends and how public pension funds can benefit from or mitigate them; the role of real assets and tactical positioning opportunities; appropriate international exposure; processes for identifying and evaluating managers; investment analysis and recommendation experience across real estate strategies, infrastructure, other assets, and co-investments; client fee discounts; performance benchmarking, including benchmark selection or development, comparisons with similar portfolios, custom benchmarks, and recommendations for INPRS’s real estate portfolio; and the firm’s ten largest general partner relationships in each real assets category.

nodes.title: Environmental, Social and Governance Matters
nodes.summary: The text asks whether the firm has an ESG policy and advocates ESG disclosure; which stewardship codes, ESG initiatives, and pledges it has adopted, any firm- or mandate-specific caveats, and how commitments affect its investment or consulting process; whether it has dedicated investment stewardship and ESG teams and how many members primarily serve each; and how much the teams overlap.

nodes.title: Exhibits
nodes.summary: The text requests exhibits covering representative investment recommendation reports for absolute return, private equity, private credit, and real assets (real estate, infrastructure, and other assets); an alternative-investment pacing model; sample quarterly and annual portfolio reports for each investment category; funds where the firm holds advisory board seats; examples of General Partner relationship reviews after board or annual meetings; and manager counts in the firm’s database by category. It also requests the firm’s latest Form ADV Part II and years registered as an investment adviser, biographies of proposed INPRS account personnel, the Code of Ethics, current insurance certificates, and the latest organizational chart.
